bull_case_summary: TSMC has Q2 FCF rising to NT$287.36bn and internally funded investment with a large liquid surplus. Round two shows a normalisation-compatible thesis: guided 56–58% margin is below Q2 peak but above prior-year Q2, without treating guidance as achieved.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts a defensible foundry purchase and quantified compensation. Inventory days of 87, Taiwan concentration, overseas capacity returns and extreme technical extension remain limits on aggressive entry rather than automatic ownership vetoes.
key_points_of_agreement: Operating and post-capex cash improvement are real.
Peak margin need not persist for a positive thesis.
Investment gains are excluded from recurring merit and cash cannot diversify geopolitical loss.
key_points_of_disagreement: How much Taiwan/capacity risk and extended entry constrain compensation at the growth-supported forward multiple.
unresolved_uncertainties: Future inventory conversion and overseas-fab returns.
Geopolitical outcomes and actual delivery of prospective guidance.
